experiment: R3 addendum: address-decoded BRAM (ram_decomp = "power", option B)
decided: 2026-10-20 (Pedro), after the G2 finding below; B+ (64 explicit banks with read enables on EN) deferred
finding_that_led_here: Synthesis ties every BRAM enable of the 64K x 32 width-sliced memory to VCC: with byte-write enables in the 32K x 1 cascaded layout, Vivado cannot map a read enable onto EN, for either coding style (results/R3/vivado/bram_enable/). opt_design then gates the lower block of each cascade pair by the address MSB; the upper blocks stay on.

So the built POWER_OPT 1 design reads the BRAM every cycle, also while the CPU sleeps: the gated design as built saves only the clock gate, B1 0.352 W (-4.0 %), B2 0.351 W (-4.3 %) at READ_WAIT 1 (idle 0.350 W).
The earlier per-state reports that set the BRAM enables to the simulated read duties (idle 0.222 W, -38 %) do not describe the built netlist and are withdrawn.

Test RAMs: with ram_decomp = "power" the memory becomes 64 address-decoded 1K x 36 blocks; each enable is a 6-bit address decode (one block per port per cycle, also while asleep); the read hold is built in fabric (about +1,950 LUT, +94 FF in a 64K x 32 test RAM).
method: Same per-state flow (r3_power_states.tcl): gated CPU clock at the simulated duty; BRAM enable static probability per block = blocks enabled per access / 64 (as built: 1; decomposed: 1/64), write enables likewise with the simulated write duty.

predictions.H9: verifier-state BRAM power at least 80 % below the as-built design (plan PLAN_R3_GATING.md section 2)

H9_cost.note: the 64-way output selector sits on the one-cycle READ_WAIT 1 read path; WNS < 0 is a stop (fallback READ_WAIT 2)

H9_idle.derivation: PL static 0.085 + clocks, signals and interface about 0.013 + BRAM: 2 block-ports always enabled at 1K x 36 (1-bit blocks cost about 0.25 W / 128 = 2 mW per block-port; a 36-bit block costs more per access, assumed 3-8x) + fabric hold/selector a few mW = 0.01-0.04 W

H9_designs.note: awake share 9.1 % (B1) and 5.8 % (B2) at READ_WAIT 1 adds only a few mW to the idle floor

predictions.H9_layout_alone: the decomposed layout without sleeping (CPU clock always on) already saves most of the BRAM power: below 0.17 W
